title: Teacher-Aware Evolution of Heuristic Programs from Learned Optimization Policies
claim: Evolution is improved by observing candidate and teacher behavior, revising programs using that evidence, then selecting offspring through Pareto retention.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, with feedback loop arrow along bottom
description: A wide three-stage diagram with panels titled Observe, Revise, and Evaluate & Select, tinted blue, red, and teal. Observe has an on-policy rollout of states s0–s3 feeding a Teacher neural-net icon. Below sits a Behavioral Evidence table comparing Program and Teacher action arrows at s1–s3, with a mismatch highlighted in red, and a Population of code-file icons. Revise has a Population Analyzer, which feeds Structural Rewrite (tree edit) and Parameter Calibration (sliders). Mechanism Fusion runs through Objective, Alignment, Analyze and Generate steps. Evaluate & Select shows Offspring code icons and a Pareto Update scatter plot, then a new population. A purple Next Generation arrow loops back along the bottom. Colored arrows link the stages, and the eye starts at the Observe title.
caption: Teacher-aware heuristic evolution. Program and teacher decisions on visited states provide behavioral evidence. Population analysis guides rewrite and calibration; fusion analyzes its selected pair. Evaluated offspring undergo Pareto retention to form the next population.
abstract: LLM-based automatic heuristic design has shown promise for generating executable heuristics for combinatorial optimization, but existing methods mainly rely on delayed endpoint performance. We propose a \emph{teacher-aware evolutionary framework} that uses independently trained learned optimization policies as behavioral teachers. Instead of deploying or imitating the teacher, our method queries it on states visited by candidate heuristic programs and uses its action preferences as local feedback for evolution. The resulting search discovers static executable heuristics guided by both task performance and teacher-derived behavioral signals. Experiments on scheduling, routing, and graph optimization benchmarks show that our method improves over performance-driven LLM heuristic evolution baselines while requiring no neural inference at deployment. These results suggest that learned optimization policies can be repurposed as behavioral feedback sources for automatic heuristic discovery.
